correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the weight-one Rota–Baxter identity to exact edge equations, uses strong connectivity to force either zero or full support, conjugates nonzero coefficients to squaring, proves the closed-walk gcd equals graph period, constructs every admissible root-of-unity solution without division by two, and evaluates the finite-field count using cyclicity of F_q^×. The explicit perfect weighted example checks the non-monomial case. Independent exact finite enumeration covers 894 graph/field combinations and the 4D weighted example; it corroborates the symbolic proof, not substitutes for it.

originality.rationale: The earliest verified motivating source (arXiv:2601.08669, January 13, 2026) analyzes weight-one Rota–Baxter operators of nilpotent maximal-nilindex evolution algebras in characteristic zero and supplies the rational recurrence. Its Theorem 5.2 does not analyze strongly connected cyclic structure graphs, arbitrary-field squaring conjugacy, or the exact root-of-unity count. The 2019 full article treats two-dimensional complex classifications, which cover a special case but do not imply the all-dimensional strongly connected graph theorem. Published research-record searches found no stronger result. The result is a new implication under the reviewed sources, with residual risk of an unlocated equivalent older graph theorem. Crucially, an accessible earlier claim already classifies the full diagonal Rota–Baxter scheme for a single oriented cycle in every field and explicitly gives the same finite-field gcd count in that case. That entire monomial cyclic subfamily is treated as prior coverage. The assessed new statement is the extension to every strongly connected branching graph and the gcd across interacting directed cycle lengths, which is not implied by a single-cycle classification.
residual_risks: The rational recurrence and its periodic-point characterization are established prior work; a general graph-period deduction could be implicit in literature not identified by targeted searches.
Some nearby papers were compared only at the abstract level; no exhaustive bibliographic uniqueness claim is made.
The count covers only diagonal operators, not the full Rota–Baxter operator variety.

A prior all-field scheme theorem covers the directed-cycle special case exactly, so the marginal novelty is limited to arbitrary strong graphs with branching and interacting cycle lengths; it is not a new cyclic count.

value.rationale: A natural graph invariant (directed period) completely determines the diagonal weight-one operator count for all strongly connected evolution-algebra graphs over every field; every nonzero edge weight becomes irrelevant. This is an all-dimensional structural classification with a sharp finite-field arithmetic dependence, including perfect non-monomial examples and characteristic-two resonances. It is motivated by the 2026 classification of the nonlinear Rota–Baxter diagonal recurrence but replaces nilpotent acyclic hypotheses with strongly connected cycles and provides exact global closing conditions. Only the diagonal sector is claimed. The interaction of distinct cycle lengths has a sharp effect beyond the prior single-cycle classification: over F8, adjoining one reverse edge to a directed 3-cycle changes the period from three to one and reduces the count from eight to two; non-monomial perfect F4 examples also fit the theorem.
